summary: High-level security and privacy review focused on data handling: retention of prompts/responses, PII/PHI considerations, encryption/KMS, audit logs, SSO/RBAC, and confirmation that Redwood does not use customer data for model training. Redwood outlined hosted vs private options and enterprise controls; agreed to provide SOC2/ISO artifacts and a written 'no-training' attestation. Next step is a technical POC for VPC/private deployment scoped by Priya and Dan.
topics: No training on customer data confirmation
Hosted vs Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) and contract/BAA
transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Samantha from Redwood, I'll hand it over to Dan, our SE, to walk through the technicals.
[00:10] Dan Park: Hey all, Dan Park here. Quick agenda, go over data handling, retention, encryption, KMS, audit logs, SSO, and then Q&A.
[00:20] Karen Li: Great, and from NovoMed we have Karen (CISO), Michael (eng manager), Priya (ML lead), Tom (procurement). We're primarily concerned about PHI, retention, and whether data could be used to train models.
[00:30] Dan Park: Totally understand, that's common. Quick preface: Redwood's product has three deployment modes—hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools), and Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). For PHI we typically recommend Private but we'll cover controls for hosted as well.
[00:45] Michael Ortega: When you say Private, do you mean full control of keys and network? We need to know where the data sits.
[00:55] Dan Park: Yes. In Private you get a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC, optional on-prem package if you need air gap. Keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM integration. For hosted, encryption at rest uses provider-managed keys by default but you can bring your own KMS in enterprise plans.
[01:12] Priya Shah: And audit logs? We need full, immutable audit trails for every request and redaction decision so we can ingest into Splunk/SIEM.
[01:22] Dan Park: We emit request-level audit logs with timestamps, request id, model/version, route, and user id. For hosted customers we retain logs and you can ship them via secure S3 export or stream to your SIEM. For Private, logs stay in your infra. We can provide syslog/HTTP forwarding.
[01:40] Karen Li: Retention periods—what's default for prompts and model outputs? We can't have PHI sitting around for months.
[01:48] Samantha Ortiz: Default is 30 days for prompts and responses for debugging and quality monitoring, but enterprise customers can opt for shorter retention, or disable retention entirely. Private deployments don't retain beyond what you configure.
[02:00] Tom Reynolds: Is that 30 days written in the TOS? We need it in contract and a process for certifying deletion.
[02:08] Samantha Ortiz: Yes, we include retention terms in the contract and can add specific deletion windows & attestations. We'll include that in the SOW.
[02:18] Priya Shah: Important question — does Redwood use customer prompts or outputs to train your models? We must be explicit.
[02:25] Dan Park: Short answer: No. We do not use customer prompts, responses, or files to train our public models.
[02:30] Priya Shah: Can you put that in writing? Legal wants an attestation.
[02:33] Samantha Ortiz: Absolutely — we'll provide a written 'no-training-on-customer-data' attestation. There are internal telemetry flows for service health but those are aggregated and stripped of PII; we can provide details on telemetry scope.
[02:45] Karen Li: What about metadata—IP addresses, user IDs—are those considered telemetry? How long are they kept?
[02:52] Dan Park: For hosted customers we retain minimal telemetry for 90 days by default (rate limiting, abuse detection), and those are pseudonymized. For enterprise plans we can customize retention and purge policies.
[03:05] Michael Ortega: Encryption specifics — at rest and in transit? TLS? KMS?
[03:10] Dan Park: In transit is TLS 1.2+ for all API calls. At rest, hosted uses AES-256 with cloud-provider managed keys unless you enable BYOK via KMS. For BYOK, we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM integrations. Keys are used to encrypt model cache and persisted artifacts.
[03:28] Priya Shah: If we bring our own keys, do you have access to the plaintext?
[03:32] Dan Park: No. With BYOK we only see ciphertext. Decryption happens in the runtime with keys accessible only by the customer-managed KMS/HSM; Redwood cannot extract keys.
[03:40] Karen Li: Ok. For HIPAA we need a BAA — do you sign BAAs for hosted or only Private?
[03:46] Samantha Ortiz: We sign BAAs for enterprise contracts. For PHI-heavy workloads we recommend Private deployment and we will include the BAA.
[03:54] Tom Reynolds: How about RBAC and SSO — we use Okta.
[03:58] Dan Park: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC; RBAC with role mapping and granular per-route permissions. For Private deployments you can enforce SSO via your IdP and we support SCIM for user provisioning.
[04:12] Priya Shah: On logging, does Redwood log full prompt content in audit logs? If so, how to prevent PHI leakage?
[04:20] Dan Park: By default, audit logs include request metadata and can include the prompt if you enable full request logging. For PHI use cases we recommend masking/redaction at the SDK or proxy level before it reaches Redwood, OR use Private deployment where you control logging. We also offer automatic PII detection redaction plug-ins for enterprise.
[04:40] Karen Li: That redaction plug-in — is it deterministic? How do we validate it?
[04:44] Dan Park: It's a configurable pipeline: detection models flag PII categories, you can choose to mask, redact, or route to a human-in-loop. For the POC we can run a sample dataset and produce metrics (precision/recall) for your regulatory team.
[04:58] Michael Ortega: Great. Any mention of model variants? We might want to fallback to smaller models for some data types.
[05:03] Dan Park: We support model variants and can route by policy. Also quantized variants for cost. For PHI we often recommend local private models to avoid egress.
[05:12] Priya Shah: A couple of noisy transcripts from other customers showed mislabelling of KV cache as 'K-V cash' in docs — just flagging for accuracy, our legal will nitpick wording.
[05:20] Samantha Ortiz: Good catch — apologies, sometimes speech-to-text messes with acronyms. We'll make sure docs use 'KV cache' and clarify terms.
[05:28] Karen Li: Regarding audit logs again, do you provide event immutability or signed logs? We need chain-of-custody for eDiscovery.
[05:36] Dan Park: We offer write-once object storage for logs in Private, and for hosted we can provide signed logs and time-stamped exports. We'll include the export workflow in the artifacts.
[05:47] Tom Reynolds: On the legal side, what is the data residency guarantee? We operate in the EU and need data to stay within EEA.
[05:54] Samantha Ortiz: We support regional hosting; hosted customers can pin their region (EU/US/APAC). For strict residency we recommend Private (VPC in your region) and contractual controls.
[06:06] Priya Shah: Do you perform background model training with synthetic or customer-derived datasets for fine-tuning? I'm worried about leakage.
[06:14] Dan Park: We do internal model research and training but not on customer data. If customers opt into data-sharing programs we get explicit consent and it's handled with extra controls. By default, customer data is excluded.
[06:26] Karen Li: Can you provide the SOC2 Type II report and ISO?
[06:29] Samantha Ortiz: Yes — we'll attach those to the follow-up email and include the SOC 2 controls mapping.
[06:36] Michael Ortega: For the POC we'll need a net-new VPC peering and perf numbers for 4k token sequences. Can you support that?
[06:43] Dan Park: Yes, we can run benchmarks in the POC. We'll need sample traffic patterns and you'll need to grant a temporary peering for testing. We'll provide a test harness.
[06:54] Priya Shah: About 'no training' — please be explicit about derivative models and embeddings. Do you keep embeddings from customer data?
[07:02] Dan Park: We don't use customer embeddings to train public models. Embeddings stored in hosted mode can be retained per retention policy; for enterprise you can host embeddings in your VPC and we won't persist them in Redwood-managed stores.
[07:16] Karen Li: Can we get a sample KMS policy? We need to show our auditors.
[07:20] Dan Park: We'll include a sample KMS policy and recommended IAM roles in the deliverables.
[07:27] Tom Reynolds: Procurement will want SLAs around deletion requests. How fast can you perform an account-wide purge?
[07:33] Samantha Ortiz: For hosted enterprise customers, account-wide purge is handled within 72 hours by default; we can contractually shorten that window. For Private, purge is under your control.
[07:44] Michael Ortega: On telemetry and anomaly detection — you mentioned aggregated data. Can you define 'aggregated' vs 'raw'?
[07:50] Dan Park: Aggregated is system metrics like latencies and token counts. Raw would be prompt content; we do not aggregate raw content for training. Telemetry that helps reliability may include hashed request ids and counts. We'll provide a telemetry spec.
[08:06] Priya Shah: Ok, let's talk about evidence — we'll need attack surface diagrams and SOC controls mapping.
[08:12] Samantha Ortiz: We'll include diagrams (network, key flow), SOC 2 mapping, and ISO artifacts in the package. Links will be provided for security docs.
[08:20] Karen Li: Are there known past incidents we should be aware of? Full disclosure to our board.
[08:27] Samantha Ortiz: We maintain a public security page with past incident summaries and mitigations; we'll share that link. Generally we have not had data breach impacting customer content.
[08:38] Michael Ortega: On redaction, it would be great if the SDK had client-side redaction hooks before sending. Is that supported?
[08:44] Dan Park: Yes — SDKs support middleware where you can run a redaction routine. We'll share example code and a redaction library for Java/Python.
[08:55] Tom Reynolds: Legally, we want indemnities around unauthorized training. Can Redwood commit there?
[09:01] Samantha Ortiz: We'll take that back to legal. We typically include standard indemnities; specifics around training and derivatives can be discussed in the contract.
[09:10] Priya Shah: For the POC metrics — if redaction affects model quality, how do we assess tradeoffs?
[09:16] Dan Park: We'll run parallel tests: raw vs redacted on synthetic PII and measure metrics (accuracy, F1). We'll produce a comparison report.
[09:27] Karen Li: Are you SOC 2 Type II?
[09:30] Samantha Ortiz: Yes, Type II, scope details vary; we'll include the full report as requested.
[09:36] Michael Ortega: Anything else on compliance like ISO or GDPR-specific items?
[09:40] Samantha Ortiz: We're ISO 27001 certified; for GDPR we provide data processing addendums (DPAs) and standard contractual clauses if needed.
[09:50] Priya Shah: Example: If a patient asks for their data to be deleted under GDPR, how do we handle that?
[09:55] Dan Park: For hosted enterprise, we process deletion requests through our support+security workflow — 72 hours to purge per contract, plus an attestation. For Private, you control the data and must follow your process.
[10:08] Tom Reynolds: For PHI in messages, what guidance do you have for minimization?
[10:12] Samantha Ortiz: Best practice: redact or tokenise PHI client-side prior to sending. If you must send PHI, use Private with BYOK and ensure logs are disabled or stored in your environment.
[10:24] Karen Li: One more on encryption: Are model checkpoints encrypted? If we use private fine-tune, will snapshots contain customer data?
[10:31] Dan Park: Model artifacts and checkpoints are encrypted at rest and only stored in customer-controlled buckets for Private. We don't persist checkpoints with customer data in hosted unless explicitly configured for a fine-tune, and then that flow is opt-in and contractually controlled.
[10:48] Michael Ortega: For the POC we'll want a test plan. Can you propose a 2-week POC with success criteria?
[10:54] Samantha Ortiz: Yes — we'll propose a plan: connectivity, 4k token latency & throughput, PII redaction accuracy, and retention verification.
[11:02] Priya Shah: On embeddings again, we need to ensure vector DBs don't leak — if you host embeddings on your managed store, are they encrypted?
[11:10] Dan Park: Yes encrypted at rest; again, enterprise can host their own vector DB in the VPC.
[11:18] Karen Li: Are there any third-party subprocessors? We need a list for our legal.
[11:22] Samantha Ortiz: We maintain a list of subprocessors and will include it. Standard cloud infra providers included.
[11:30] Michael Ortega: Ok, sounds good. Any closing security notes?
[11:34] Dan Park: We'll provide a deliverable zip: SOC2, ISO cert, KMS sample policies, network diagrams, telemetry spec, redaction code samples, and the no-training attestation.
[11:45] Samantha Ortiz: Recap of next steps: I'll send the certs and attestation; Dan will send technical docs and schedule a POC; Priya and Michael to provide sample traffic. Tom will start procurement.
[11:56] Karen Li: Thanks, we'll review and get back with dates.
[12:00] Samantha Ortiz: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD with links.
[12:05] [call ends]
